sentences.text: Cobelodus was a predator that grew up to 1.5 to 2 meters long. It possessed unusual 30 cm long, flexible cartilaginous tentacles sprouting from its pectoral fins.
The type specimen, originally assigned to the species Styptobasis aculeata, was discovered by Edward Drinker Cope in the Illinois Basin black coal shales.
Rainer Zangerl reassigned the species S. aculeata to the genus Cobelodus in 1973.
Cobelodus is classified in the extinct order Symmoriida. Its parent group is the family Symmoriidae.
Cobelodus lived from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian period, specifically between the Visean and Artinskian stages, from 335.4 to 283.3 million years ago.
